title: Finite graded cohomology over a finite type algebra on a proper algebraic space
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $B=\bigoplus_{k\geq0}B_k$ be a commutative unital graded $A$-algebra: $B_k$ are $A$-submodules, $B_kB_l\subseteq B_{k+l}$, $1\in B_0$, and $A\to B$ lands in $B_0$. Assume $B$ is a finite type $A$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a proper morphism of algebraic spaces [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-trf-algebraic-space, def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Put $\mathcal B=f^*\widetilde B=\bigoplus_{k\geq0}\mathcal B_k$ with $\mathcal B_k=f^*\widetilde{B_k}$, where $\widetilde B$ is the quasi-coherent algebra associated to $B$ on the affine base, and $f^*$ is tensor pullback on the small etale ringed topoi [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors, lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence]. Let $\mathcal G=\bigoplus_{r\geq0}\mathcal G_r$ be a graded $\mathcal B$-module whose pieces are quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules on the small etale site [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Here grading means restriction-compatible $\mathcal O_X$-bilinear maps $\mathcal B_k\times\mathcal G_r\to\mathcal G_{r+k}$ obeying the unit and associativity laws; the direct sums are in module sheaves. Assume $\mathcal G$ is of finite type over $\mathcal B$: etale locally there are finitely many homogeneous sections $s_i$ of degrees $d_i$ such that every homogeneous section is locally a finite sum of products $b_i s_i$ with $b_i\in\mathcal B_{r-d_i}$ in degree $r\geq d_i$. For $b\in B_k$, let $\mu_{k,r}(b):\mathcal G_r\to\mathcal G_{r+k}$ be multiplication by its pulled-back section. For every $q\geq0$, using right derived global sections of underlying additive sheaves [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], the additive group $\bigoplus_{r\geq0}H^q(X,\mathcal G_r)$ is a finitely generated $B$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] with action
$$\left(\sum_k b_k\right)(x_r)_r=\left(\sum_{k+r=d}H^q(X,\mu_{k,r}(b_k))(x_r)\right)_{d\geq0}.$$
Both inputs have finite support, and the degree-zero action of $a\in A$ is the cohomology map induced by multiplication by $f^\sharp(a)$ on each piece.

source.place: Tag 08AT, lemma-graded-finiteness; the graded cohomology action is written explicitly. Its direct-sum interpretation follows from Tag 073E (lemma-colimits), applied to finite partial sums, since a proper space over an affine scheme is quasi-compact and quasi-separated.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal G=\bigoplus_r\mathcal G_r$, forgetting the grading temporarily. By [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-kernels-colimits], this module sheaf is quasi-coherent. The stipulated multiplication maps give the $\mathcal B$-action: sheafifying the bilinear maps from finite partial sums gives the action on the direct sums, and the given equations give its unit and associativity. On an etale neighbourhood with homogeneous generators $s_1,\ldots,s_n$, the map $\mathcal B^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal G$, $(b_i)\mapsto\sum_i b_i s_i$, is locally surjective. Indeed a section of a module-sheaf direct sum is locally a finite sum of homogeneous sections, and each is locally generated as in the hypothesis. Thus $\mathcal G$ is finite type over $\mathcal B$ as an ungraded module.

source.place: Tag 08AT, lemma-graded-finiteness, quasi-coherent graded module viewed without grading

proof.text: Set $T=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $Y=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}T$, with projections $p:Y\to X$ and $h:Y\to T$. The algebra $B$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], and $h$ is proper by [lem-sfb-space-proper-base-change]. Properness as defined in [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties] gives finite type and separatedness. For each etale scheme chart of $Y$ its composite to $T$ is locally of finite type, so [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] makes it locally Noetherian. Thus $Y$ is locally Noetherian. Properness over an affine base also gives quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of both $Y$ and $X$: the base is quasi-compact, and their absolute diagonals are composites of closed relative diagonals with base changes of the affine base's quasi-compact diagonal.

source.place: Tag 08AT, first paragraph; algebra.tex Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence); spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 04WP (lemma-base-change-proper), with local Noetherianity tested on charts

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-space-relative-spec-correspondence] and its arbitrary base-change clause, $Y$ over $X$ is the affine space associated to $f^*\widetilde B=\mathcal B$, and $p_*\mathcal O_Y\cong\mathcal B$ as algebras. Apply [lem-sfb-space-affine-module-correspondence] to the quasi-coherent underlying module from step 1 and this algebra action. It supplies a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module $F$ and an isomorphism $p_*F\cong\mathcal G$ of $\mathcal B$-modules. In particular the isomorphism respects the multiplication maps by each section of $\mathcal B$.

source.place: Tag 08AT, relative spectrum identification and module correspondence; spaces-morphisms.tex Tags 081V and 08AI

proof.text: Here is the finite-type verification omitted in 08AT. Refine the neighbourhoods of the generators in step 1 to affine etale charts $U\to X$. The epimorphism $\mathcal B_U^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal G_U$ corresponds under [lem-sfb-space-affine-module-correspondence], compatible with this etale restriction, to an epimorphism $\mathcal O_{Y_U}^{\oplus n}\to F|_{Y_U}$. To check epimorphisms it suffices to take their cokernel: the equivalence preserves cokernels, and these are the sheaf cokernels because they remain quasi-coherent by [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-kernels-colimits]. Thus $F$ is locally finitely generated on an etale cover of $Y$. On each scheme chart of $Y$, finite type and quasi-coherence imply coherence by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth], since the chart is locally Noetherian by step 2. The coherence criterion in [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-groupoid-equivalence] then makes $F$ coherent on $Y$.

source.place: Tag 08AT, omitted finite-type verification; Tag 07UB (lemma-coherent-Noetherian), etale chart criterion

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-space-proper-coherent-higher-images], $R^qh_*F$ is coherent on $T$. In the affine chart $T\to T$ its section module is therefore finite over $B$, by the explicit coherence convention of that cited statement. Since $h$ is qcqs, [lem-sfb-space-affine-base-higher-image-sections] identifies this module with module-derived $H^q(Y,F)$, naturally in $F$. Multiplication by each $b\in B$ commutes with this comparison. Finally [lem-sfb-ringed-site-global-module-abelian-cohomology] identifies module-derived cohomology with the cohomology of the underlying additive sheaf, naturally and linearly over global functions. Hence $H^q(Y,F)$ in the convention of the item is a finite $B$-module for every $q\ge0$.

source.place: Tag 08AS, lemma-proper-over-affine-cohomology-finite, as used in the last sentence of 08AT; Tag 03FD for the module/additive comparison

proof.text: Since $p$ is affine, [lem-sfb-space-affine-cohomology] gives $H^q(X,p_*F)\cong H^q(Y,F)$. This comparison commutes with multiplication by every $b\in B$: the module Leray spectral sequence [lem-sfb-ringed-site-leray-spectral-sequence] is natural in module maps, and [lem-sfb-space-affine-module-higher-image-vanishing] kills its positive rows, so its edge commutes with the endomorphism $b:F\to F$. The natural module/additive comparison [lem-sfb-ringed-site-global-module-abelian-cohomology] gives the same assertion in underlying-additive cohomology. Under $p_*F\cong\mathcal G$, the endomorphism $p_*(b)$ is multiplication by the pulled-back section of $\mathcal B$. Consequently $H^q(X,\mathcal G)$, with this action, is isomorphic as a $B$-module to the finite module of step 5.

source.place: Tag 08AT, affine cohomology comparison; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0732 (lemma-Leray), naturality

proof.text: The finite subsets $E\subset\mathbb N$ form a small filtered poset, and $\mathcal G$ is the colimit of $\bigoplus_{r\in E}\mathcal G_r$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] the same colimit description holds after forgetting to abelian sheaves. Apply [lem-sfb-space-cohomology-filtered-colimit], since $X$ is qcqs by step 2. Cohomology is additive on finite direct sums, so the resulting canonical map is an isomorphism $$\Phi:\bigoplus_{r\ge0}H^q(X,\mathcal G_r)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(X,\mathcal G).$$ It is characterized on the $r$th summand by the cohomology map induced by the sheaf injection $\iota_r:\mathcal G_r\to\mathcal G$.

source.place: Tag 073E (lemma-colimits), applied to finite partial sums; direct-sum interpretation of 08AT

proof.text: For homogeneous $b\in B_k$, its multiplication $m_b$ on $\mathcal G$ obeys $m_b\iota_r=\iota_{r+k}\mu_{k,r}(b)$. Apply the additive cohomology functor: $$H^q(m_b)\Phi\iota_r=\Phi\iota_{r+k}H^q(\mu_{k,r}(b)).$$ Every $b\in B$ and every element of the cohomology direct sum have finite homogeneous support. Expanding both as finite sums therefore gives exactly the convolution formula in the statement, and proves that $\Phi$ is $B$-linear for that formula. The unit and associativity laws follow by applying functoriality to $m_1=\mathrm{id}$ and $m_bm_c=m_{bc}$; additivity gives the distributive laws. If $b$ is the image of $a\in A$, its action on each piece is the cohomology map of multiplication by $f^\sharp(a)$, by the given scalar-action hypothesis. Finally a finite generating set for the module of step 6 pulls back through $\Phi$ to a finite generating set of the displayed graded module, as required.
